title: 82626B0054-BEDC-PS-318 Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station
agency_path: City of New York > Environmental Protection
description_text:
PS-318: Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station Paerdegat pumping station is located in Brooklyn, New York at 6002 Flatlands Ave, Brooklyn, New York that flows to the Coney Island Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility. The Pumping Station was constructed in 1932 with an upgrade completed in 1995. The station currently has a designed flow capacity of 57 million gallons per day (MGD) wet weather flow and 22.8 MGD dry weather flow. The existing station is in need of State of Good Repair (SOGR) upgrades in order to improve compliance with DEPs SOPs and design guidelines. Specifically, areas needing SOGR improvements include replacing existing pumps, placing wet well elevation monitoring system, new mechanical, HVAC, electrical, I&C systems, resiliency upgrades, provide permanent emergency fuel generator and fuel storage, replace crane electrification system, rehab wet well structure, reconstruction of floors, walls, and ceilings, replace clay tile and membrane roofing, replace building façade walls, windows, floors, and brick fence, replace plumbing and fixtures in bathroom, replace existing force main, install new parallel force main, extend spillway, replace the gate wall thimbles, constructing two influent chambers for emergency bypass system, install cameras for remote monitoring, relocation of station identification sign, and replace of vintage wood gate.

For the purposes of this report and for internal NYCDEP coordination, all references to the pumping station will refer to the Paerdegat pumping station to be consistent with the PS-DES-5 contract language. Paerdegat is owned and operated by the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (NYCDEP) Bureau of Wastewater Treatment (BWT) This Competitive Sealed Bid (RFx') is being released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal.
